label: The Port Desert

terrain.note: Issue #77: the home planet is a whole ball of sphere_radius metres (src/systems/planets/planet_sphere.gd): sand all the way round, walkable everywhere, up turns with the ground. The flat keys below are what the square desert used and are kept only for worlds without a sphere.

landmarks.note: Wreck field: three more of the same class came down all round the ball, each lying its own way: this one 6 km out south-west, nearly flat on its belly with its decks let down; _3 9 km out north, over the curve of the ball, sunk past its middle so you walk in through the breach on the sand; _4 on the far side of the planet, 1.4 km from the point straight through it from the port, nose-down at 26 degrees and listing to starboard. All 'kind': 'wreck' (src/systems/world/starcruiser_wreck.gd). Pose: 'yaw_deg' (heading), 'pitch_deg' (the bow's dive, the original's 34 down to nearly flat), 'roll_deg' (a list onto one flank), 'bury_height' (how far the middle of the hull stands above the sand; below zero and the middle is under it). The decks, ramps and bridge are one design that keeps its place under the dorsal hatch at any pitch, and what joins them to the hold is worked out from the pose: the stern ramp where the floor meets the starboard deck, else a climb ramp up the starboard side to the low balcony; variant 'deck_drop' lowers the decks for a flat one. 'variant' also makes each a little different: a deck or ramp fallen away, a radiator gone, other railings knocked out (StarcruiserWreck.VARIANT_KEYS). Their droids and the prize crate on each one's bridge platform: droids/droids.json 'wreck'.sites, pickups/port_town.json 'site_crates'.

The racers' outpost: the old abandoned outpost, taken over by the basin crew (content/core/locations/outpost.json). It sits in the Basin Run's infield, about 150 m in from the racing line all round and 165 m from the start line, its gate (+x) turned toward the start. Planet layout spread: the outpost, the Basin Run and the Blue Basin droid relay moved together, 3.9 km out south-south-east (turned round the ball as one piece, so the course keeps its shape and the outpost its place in it). 'clear' keeps the rocks off its yard.

Issue #295: Skrugs's post, a different place in each town layout ('layouts', resolved once by CoreContent.resolve_layout where the world is loaded). Round port: his yard inside the wall right behind the cantina (skrugs_post_round, turned so +x faces the back lane). Square port: out in the sand past its back gate, where it stood before issue #237 (skrugs_post, +x facing the gate).

Issue #295: Skrugs's sand ramp, out past the back gate (it was part of his post until his round-port yard moved inside the wall). Round port: where it stood when his post was out in the sand. Square port: where it always was, past his post. Rises toward -z.

Planet layout spread: only this one (the dry wash, 0.85 km out) stays near the port, by the Red Wind's loop. The other six are spread round the whole planet: the broken ridge (mid) 2.9 km north-north-east (still the second nearest, so the story's first heist is a short drive), the dust gap (southwest) 3.7 km south-south-west, the old well (south) 5.6 km north-east under a mountain, the glass flats (west) 8.2 km west, the deep dunes (far) 11.8 km east and the salt pan (north) 11.6 km south, both over the curve on the far side. Each is turned so its door (+x) faces the port.
Issue #187: the four outposts round the other sides of the town. Planet layout spread: see remnant_outpost_near's note for where each stands now.

Ranch villages: three walled yards, each a Remnant outpost with a few houses, four merchant stands (gear, food, the fence, droids; no speeders) and armed locals round a fire. Two far out west (Saltpan and Windbreak), the third out east under the Remnant's cruiser, beyond the first wreck. 3.5 to 4.5 km from the port: well below its horizon, and past the 1500 m the ranches draw their buildings to (src/systems/world/ranches.gd), so nothing of them is drawn at the start. Each is two landmarks at the same spot: the outpost (remnant_outpost_<name>, one of Story.OUTPOSTS) and the ranch round it (ranch_<name>). Turned so the gate (+x) faces the port.

Races 4 and 5: the two ranch villages on the far side of the planet, Cragfall (the crag crew's, by the Crooked Mile, 12.6 km round the ball from the port) and Farleap (the leap crew's, by the Far Leaps, nearly 14 km round, the furthest place there is), each by the far mountains a race runs through. Built like the three other ranch villages (each two landmarks at one spot), but turned so the gate (+x) faces their crew's start line, not the port (half a planet away).

The droid post nearest the port: about 310 m straight out from the front gate, a kilometre closer than it first stood, so its hut and tall array show through the gate from the street inside. Its counter faces the gate.

Issue #193: the Remnant's star cruiser, holding orbit 7 km up over map point 'at' (6.5 km east along the ground, 75 degrees round the ball): below the port's horizon, in plain sight from space. It is level with the port (its decks square to world up, with its own gravity aboard) and its bay is turned toward the port; yaw_deg turns it about its up. 7 km (was 4.6): three km past the edge of space, so the escort fight runs most of the way there. Its shapes are src/systems/world/cruiser_hull.gd, everything else content/core/cruiser/remnant_cruiser.json.

detail.note: Issue #46: less to draw (and run) the higher you fly. Read by src/systems/world/altitude_detail.gd. Each tier holds once the viewer is 'above' that many metres over sea level and lets go 'hysteresis' metres lower. off: render features (sdfgi, ssil, ssao, volumetric, shadows). hide: node groups the town registers (people = bodies, the cantina owner and their brains; props = lamps, banners, boulders). SDFGI goes first: it rebuilds whenever a fast camera moves, which is what made flying laggy.

sight.note: Issue #693: build by sight. A no-fade handoff (flying in from open space) builds nothing the ship could not see yet. Read by src/systems/world/sight_gate.gd and scenes/town_demo.gd _build_by_sight. range_m: never built further from the camera than this; horizon_margin_m: built this far before it would crest the curve of the ball; release_m: kept this much further out once in (no flicker on the edge). hold: build steps that wait till the ship is under that many metres over the ground (they are only drawn from close by), in layers on the way down, big to small, so they never land on the same frames; a step must not be held lower than one it needs (the mechanic needs the speeders). Outposts come in one by one as they could be seen.

detail.ground_detail_note: The mid ring (the 1 km square of fine sand under the camera, src/systems/look/planet_terrain.gd) is built only below this many metres over the ground, with the props tier; higher up only the whole ball is drawn, so the square is not seen from kilometres out. 0 = always.

note: IP-neutral. The world around the port, for flying: where the desert ends and the planet curves away, the landmarks set in it, and the height where the atmosphere ends. The desert's shape is the town's DesertTerrain (src/systems/look/desert_terrain.gd) and its mesas and hoodoos are content/look/desert_landforms.json; this file does not repeat them. terrain.extent = the desert's half-size (its own extent wins when the desert is built); beyond it the ground is skirt_height falling away on a sphere of planet_radius from curve_from. Altitude is measured above that curved surface, so space_altitude is the same everywhere. Issue #46: planet_radius halved (120 km to 60 km), a smaller world whose horizon curves in sooner, so less of it is ever drawn. Colours: content/look/world.json.
